examples.problem_statement: Multiply 41 by 41 using Vedic method with working base 50.

solution.description: Both factors are 41, which sits near 50, so take 50 as the working base. Because 50 is half of the theoretical base 100, a division by 2 will be needed later on the left-hand part.
Measure the factor against the working base: 41 is 9 short of 50, so its deviation is -9. Both factors are 41, so both carry the same deviation.
Cross-subtract: take the deviation 9 away from the other factor, 41 - 9 = 32. This is the left-hand part before the working-base adjustment.
Multiply the two deviations: (-9) x (-9) = 81. Two negatives give a positive, and 81 fills the two digits that the theoretical base 100 allows on the right.
Because the working base 50 is half of 100, halve the left part: 32 divided by 2 is 16. Only the left-hand part is adjusted this way.
Set the adjusted left part 16 in front of the right part 81 to read 41 x 41 = 1681.
